subject: astronomy
title: Black Holes: Event Horizon and Schwarzschild Radius
welcome_lead: Where gravity is so strong that nothing — not even light — escapes.
meta_desc: A-Level Astronomy: Schwarzschild radius, event horizon and singularity.
final_note: The event horizon is a one-way membrane in spacetime.

concepts.def: A region where escape velocity exceeds c.
Boundary of no return around a black hole.
Rs = 2GM/c^2 — radius of a non-rotating event horizon.
Predicted point of infinite curvature at a black hole's centre.
Speed needed to escape a body's gravity.

walkthroughs.body_html: Einstein's general relativity (1915) treats gravity as curvature of spacetime. Solving the field equations for a non-rotating mass gives the Schwarzschild solution — and predicts black holes.
Rs = 2GM/c^2. For one solar mass, Rs is about 3 km; for Earth, about 9 mm. Inside the event horizon, no signal can reach the outside universe.
Classical general relativity predicts a singularity of infinite density at the centre. Quantum gravity is expected to modify this, but no observation has reached inside an event horizon.
